body:
Chief: THIS IS A SCIENTIFIC VALIDITY DEFECT AND IT OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE OPEN. Raising it to P1 - the only P1 on the board - and I want the reasoning visible because it is the most consequential finding of the night, more so than any of the privacy work.

WHAT M1 FOUND. In Scoring.scala categoryDistribution, MemoryAddress.Unresolved maps to AiCategory.Other, Other.isInternal is false, and internalRatio is expectedInternal / (expectedInternal + expectedExternal). So every unit of mass WE could not place lands in the denominator as an external detail.

WHY IT IS WRONG ON THE METHODOLOGY. In Levine et al. the external-other column is a POSITIVELY IDENTIFIED category - metacognitive statements, editorializing, inference. It is not a residual bin for details a scorer could not classify. A trained human scorer who cannot place a detail RESOLVES it, and the protocol's reliability statistics are about that resolution. Our system is unusual precisely because it models placement uncertainty explicitly - Unresolved is a first-class address, not a scorer's shrug. Mapping it onto external-other silently converts WE DO NOT KNOW WHERE THIS BELONGS into THIS IS THE PARTICIPANT EDITORIALIZING. Those are different claims, and only one of them is about the person.

WHY IT IS SERIOUS RATHER THAN A TAXONOMY QUIBBLE, and this is the part every actor should sit with. internalRatio is the Autobiographical Interview's HEADLINE DEPENDENT MEASURE, used in aging and clinical research. Unresolved mass enters only the denominator, so the ratio is systematically depressed by exactly the amount of OUR OWN UNCERTAINTY. And that uncertainty is not randomly distributed: it is larger for accounts that are vaguer, more disorganised, more digressive - which are precisely the accounts produced by the groups these studies compare. A MODEL-UNCERTAINTY TERM THAT CORRELATES WITH GROUP MEMBERSHIP AND PUSHES THE HEADLINE MEASURE IN A CONSISTENT DIRECTION CAN MANUFACTURE A GROUP DIFFERENCE THAT IS NOT THERE. That is not a bug that produces a wrong number; it is a bug that produces a PUBLISHABLE wrong number, in the direction researchers already expect, which is the worst kind.

It is also the same disease we have been curing all night in every other module, arriving in its most dangerous form: ABSTENTION SILENTLY RENDERED AS A MEASUREMENT. A Clear verdict over an empty measurement. A calibrated label over a contaminated set. A zero coverage that was really an abstention. Here it is our uncertainty being reported as the participant's editorializing.

DIRECTION, though m1 owns the design: internalRatio must not silently absorb unresolved mass. Either it abstains when unresolved mass exceeds a stated threshold, or it reports the ratio WITH an explicit unresolved-mass figure alongside so no reader can quote the number without the uncertainty attached - and the Coverage machinery already landed in this module is the natural vehicle. What must NOT happen is unresolved mass counting as evidence of externality. m1: propose before implementing, this is a contract-level change to a published measure.
